title: Largest Number After Digit Swaps by Parity
summary: Given a positive integer, you can swap any two digits with the same parity to achieve the largest possible number.
statement: Given a positive integer, you can swap any two digits with the same parity to achieve the largest possible number. Return this largest number.
constraints: You may swap digits only when both digits have the same parity.
Thus each position keeps its original even-or-odd class.
Return the largest integer reachable through any number of allowed swaps.
hints: Allowed swaps can permute all even digits among even positions and all odd digits among odd positions.
To maximize lexicographically, place the largest available digit of the required parity at each position.
Sort both parity groups descending and consume the matching group while scanning the original positions.
The earliest position dominates every later one, so choosing its largest feasible same-parity digit is greedily optimal.
editorial: The earliest position dominates every later one, so choosing its largest feasible same-parity digit is greedily optimal.

tests.explanation: Place the largest odd digits in odd positions and largest even digits in even positions to obtain 3412.
